title: What We Know About the Voynich Manuscript
summary: Reddy and Knight compare the manuscript with natural-language texts using character and word prediction and page-level statistics. Most experiments focus on the Biological and Stars sections of Currier B, with additional comparisons for the full manuscript.
established: In the tenfold word-type test in Table 2, the Currier B bigram letter predictor gets 40.02% correct versus 14.65% from unigrams. The bigram figures are 22.62% for English, 24.78% for Arabic and 38.92% for Pinyin.

In the whole-word test in Table 4, the Currier B unigram and bigram hit rates are 2.30% and 2.50%. Table 5 reports a 31.8% relative improvement for predicting the first character from the preceding word's last character, compared with 31.1% for English and 26.8% for Arabic in that one-character condition.

Table 6 compares page entropy with a scrambled document cut to the original page lengths. The normalized difference is 0.033 for Currier B, 0.037 for the Wall Street Journal, 0.069 for English Genesis and 0.025 for their Quran sample. The reference texts use different definitions of a page.
